THE DH-SUFFIXED TWIN OF THE ACCEPTED 'PurposeCode' ROW ABOVE, missed only because this list keys on exact fieldId. Added 2026-09-04 after it blocked EVERY provider: CHECK 5 is read by enforce on all 20, so this single field turned the whole portfolio BLOCKED and report_mission_status to 0 of 20. FormInput in 12 providers (a 1-char code prefilled 'C'), FormSelect in CA_eSUN (a value-list dropdown, attributeTypeId=DEX_INQUIRY_PURPOSE_CODE). CA_eSUN IS THE CORRECT ONE AND IT WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: its engineering-built v1.0 -- the configuration running live at San Diego Sheriff -- carries 5 FormSelect purpose controls, which is precisely why DEX-1313 exists to convert that DROPDOWN to radio buttons. Building it as FormInput would delete the officer-selectable purpose code SDSO actually uses. Same adjudication as the PurposeCode row: provider metadata decides, and both are valid.

SCOPED TO SC_SLED ONLY -- a FormInput RegistrationState anywhere else is still a FAIL, and that matters because all 21 providers build this control. THE LAST SURVIVOR OF THREE SUCH ROWS: 'raceCode' and 'SexCode' sat here too and were DELETED at v1.10 because their premise stopped being true -- both are proper dropdowns again. Keeping a row whose stated condition no longer exists is the exact defect audit_registry_currency exists to catch, so they went rather than being left to read like live adjudications. WHY THOSE TWO CAME BACK AND THIS ONE HAS NOT: LIMITATION #28 only breaks the attributeTypeId + codeTypeProvider REVERSE-LOOKUP pattern. A control carrying its own codeTypeCategory/codeTypeSource resolves locally and sends the SELECTED CODE, so #28 has nothing to break -- which is why SC_SLED's GunMake, GunCaliber and ArticleTypeCode dropdowns have always worked on their own two-QIF entities. Sex now uses the documented CommSys-only fallback (NIBRS_SEX|NIBRS, FIELD_REFERENCE Section 4) and Race uses NIBRS_RACE|NIBRS, the shape MD_METERS (ALL-PASS, 47 logs) and LA_LEMS already ship. THE SAME ESCAPE IS AVAILABLE FOR STATE (NJ_NIBRS_STATE|NJ_NIBRS, 'sends 2-letter code') AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN HERE YET: it has ZERO carriers portfolio-wide (all 69 state dropdowns use attributeTypeId='STATE'), and whether an NJ_NIBRS source resolves on a non-NJ tenant is unverifiable from this repo -- an empty dropdown would be WORSE than this type-in, because an officer can at least type 'SC'. v1.10 runs that experiment on ONE control only, the Wanted Person plate state, so a single import discriminates; converting Boat in the same bump would double the exposure and teach nothing extra. IF THE WANTED STATE DROPDOWN POPULATES, convert this control the same way and delete this row too. BACKGROUND on why Boat is multi-QIF at all: v1.8 moved AdministrativeMessage to targetEntity='Boat' because Rob asked for that tab LAST ('put admin at the end like i asked'), and the tab rule measured off the v1.7 tenant says a tab is last only if it sits on the LAST entity. Boat's State was the rescue pattern -- Sel with attributeTypeId='STATE' (which ALONE sends the platform's internal numeric row id, AP #1) plus codeTypeProvider='NCIC' on the BoatQuery attribute -- so keeping the dropdown would have put a numeric id on the wire where SC expects a state code. Cost measured before choosing: State is any[]-ONLY on both Boat combos (QBBQ.H, QBBQ.R), a pure optional and NOT a routing discriminator, so no BUILD_RULES 24 exposure. SC_SLED also builds RegistrationState as a FormSelect on Vehicle and Person, both single-QIF, and those are UNAFFECTED -- this divergence is intra-provider as well as cross-provider.
